claims.text: AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock has a multiphase microstructure.
AlCrFeNiSi powder has laser absorptivity properties typical of high-alloy additive-manufacturing feedstocks.
The proposed LOAAM-FB process uses 5–10 µs laser dwell times and a scanning speed of approximately 500 mm/s.
Dynamic feedback adjustment of laser modulation will maintain melt-pool stability and complete fusion.
The process is intended to operate in an inert atmosphere with substrate preheating of approximately 200°C.
The applicable geometry consists of miniature components with sub-10 mm features.
The specified processing window will produce rapid local solidification and improve thermal management.
Ultrafast laser modulation combined with real-time feedback will produce a consistently uniform melt pool.
A uniform melt pool will minimize steep thermal gradients.
Minimized thermal gradients will generate a fine-grained, homogeneous microstructure with substantially lower residual stress.
Rapid oscillation of laser energy limits the material's exposure time at high temperature.
Limiting high-temperature exposure reduces thermal gradients and permits localized stress relaxation during solidification.
In-situ melt-pool monitoring and feedback will prevent balling and lack-of-fusion defects associated with microsecond-scale modulation.
LOAAM-FB components will have significantly lower residual thermal stress than components made by conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
LOAAM-FB components will have improved yield strength and ductility relative to the conventional-process baseline.
LOAAM-FB will reduce post-processing requirements relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
Conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing typically produces higher residual stresses and coarser microstructures and requires complex post-processing heat treatments.
The efficacy of LOAAM-FB may diminish for larger geometries or substantially different alloy systems.
